Rashi on Niddah 68b:10:1.hebrew: מי איכא למאן דאמר כו' - והא אפילו רבנן בתראי בשני שלה הוא דקאמרי, אבל בראשון, דהוי פתיחת מעיינה, ליכא למאן דאמר דאם בדקה בצהרים ומצאה טהור, דתהוי הפרשה:
Rashi on Niddah 68b:10:1.english: Is there anyone who says, etc. - For behold, even the latter Rabbis [in the mishna] said [this] only regarding her second [day], but on the first [day], which is the opening of her spring, there is no one who says that if she examined [herself] at midday and found [herself] pure, that it should be [considered] a cessation [of flow].

Rashi on Niddah 68b:13:1.english: And I erred in that I did not ask - For had I asked, they would have declared [her] pure.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:14:1.english: Initially, what did he think - That he did not want to ask.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:15:1.hebrew: הזב והזבה - שפסקו והתחילו לספור ז', ובדקו יום ראשון ושביעי כו':
Rashi on Niddah 68b:15:1.english: The zav and the zava - Who ceased [discharging] and began to count seven [clean days], and examined [themselves on] the first and seventh [days], etc.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:15:2.english: Rabbi Akiva says: They have only the seventh [day] - Lest they saw [a discharge] in the interim and invalidated their first count.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:17:1.hebrew: אי אתה מודה בזב שראה קרי - בימי ספירו, שאינו מונה אותו יום, דקיימא לן דסותר יום א' ומונה לסירוגין:
Rashi on Niddah 68b:17:1.english: Do you not concede with regard to a zav who experienced a seminal emission - [That is,] during the days of his counting, that he does not count that day, as we maintain that it cancels one day and he counts at intervals.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:17:2.hebrew: ונזיר שהילך סככות ופרעות - שהן ספק אהל, אין אותו יום עולה למנין נזירותו, ונמצא שמונה ל' יום של סתם נזירות בסירוגין:
Rashi on Niddah 68b:17:2.english: And a nazirite who walked [under] overhanging boughs and protrusions - As they are an uncertain tent, that day does not count toward the tally of his naziriteship, and it turns out that he counts the thirty days of an unspecified naziriteship intermittently.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:18:1.english: There - [This refers to] a zav who experienced a seminal emission.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:18:2.hebrew: לטמאה בה כתיב - זאת תורת הזב ואשר תצא ממנו שכבת זרע וגו' (ויקרא טו). מה זיבה סותרת, אף קרי סותר. אי מה זיבה סותרת הכל, אף קרי סותר הכל? ת"ל: לטמאה בה - אין לך סתירה אלא בטומאתה האמור בה: מה טומאת קרי יום אחד, אף סתירתה יום אחד:
Rashi on Niddah 68b:18:2.english: "To be defiled therein" is written - "This is the law of the zav, and of him from whom an emission of semen goes out, etc." (Leviticus 15). Just as zivah overturns [the count of clean days], so too a seminal emission overturns [the count]. If [so, might one think that] just as zivah overturns everything, so too a seminal emission should overturn everything? The verse states: "To be defiled therein" — you have no overturning other than according to its [own] impurity stated regarding it: just as the impurity of a seminal emission is [for] one day, so too its overturning is [for] one day.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:18:3.english: And if due to confusion - So that one does not come to count intermittently in [a case of] actual zivah.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:19:1.hebrew: אהל מעליא בעינן - אין נזיר מטמא אלא באהל מת ודאי, כדכתיב (במדבר ו׳:ט׳): וכי ימות מת עליו — במחוורת עליו, כדאמר בכיצד צולין (פסחים פא:):
Rashi on Niddah 68b:19:1.english: We require a full-fledged tent - A nazirite becomes ritually impure only through the tent of a definite corpse, as it is written (Numbers 6:9): "And if a person dies beside him" — [meaning, when it is] clear to him, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] "Keitzad Tzolin" (Pesachim 81b).

Rashi on Niddah 68b:19:2.hebrew: ורבנן גזור ביה - לסתור אותו יום. וא"ת: אתי לאיחלופי באהל מת גמור, ולא יסתור אלא יום א':
Rashi on Niddah 68b:19:2.english: And the Sages decreed regarding it - To forfeit that day. And if you say: One might come to confuse [it] with a full-fledged tent of a corpse, and forfeit only one day?

Rashi on Niddah 68b:19:3.english: [A matter of] rabbinic law with [a matter of] Torah law - A tent of uncertainty [instituted by] rabbinic law will not be confused with a tent [mandated by] Torah law.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:1:1.hebrew: וכן תנא לוי במתניתא - אסיפא דמתני' תני הכי: בדקה ז' שחרית ומצאה טמאה, ובין השמשות לא הפרישה, ואחר הימים — בין בדקה ומצאה טהורה, בין בדקה ומצאה טמאה — הרי זו ספק זבה:
Rashi on Niddah 68b:1:1.english: And Levi taught similarly in a baraita - Regarding the latter clause of the mishna, he taught as follows: If she examined herself on the seventh [day in the] morning and found herself ritually impure, and at twilight did not perform a separation [examination], and after [several] days — whether she examined and found herself ritually pure or whether she examined and found herself ritually impure — she is an uncertain zava.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:20:1.hebrew: אבל הכא אי חיישינן - ולא תמנה יום שבינתיים משום דלמא חזאי, בספק אתי למיחלף בודאי, דאמרינן: מדלא מנינן הני ימים, ודאי חזאי בינתיים, וקא מניא לראשון, ואתיא למנות ודאי רואה בסירוגין:
Rashi on Niddah 68b:20:1.english: But here, if we are concerned - And she should not count an intermediate day because perhaps she saw [blood], [then] an uncertainty will come to be confused with certainty. For [people] will say: "Since we do not count these days, [it must be that] she definitely saw [blood] in the interim, and yet she counts the first [day]." And [thus] she will come to count [clean days even when] definitely seeing [blood] intermittently.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:21:1.hebrew: נראין דברי ר"א מדברי רבי יהושע - דכיון דחייש רבי יהושע לשמא ראה בינתיים, היה לו לסתור אף הראשון:
Rashi on Niddah 68b:21:1.english: The statement of Rabbi Eliezer appears [more correct] than the statement of Rabbi Yehoshua - For since Rabbi Yehoshua is concerned that perhaps he saw [a discharge] in the interim, he should have overturned even the first [day].

Rashi on Niddah 68b:21:2.english: And the statement of Rabbi Akiva [appears more correct] than the statement of all of them - For he requires [the days to be both] counted and examined.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:22:1.hebrew: יום שמיני - כבר עברו ימי הספירה, ולא היה סופן בטהרה, דלא בדקה יום ז':
Rashi on Niddah 68b:22:1.english: The eighth day - The days of counting have already passed, and their conclusion was not in purity, as she did not examine [herself on] the seventh day.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:2:1.hebrew: לומר שאינה מטמאה מעת לעת - בפ' בנות כותים (לעיל נדה לט.) קתני: כל אחד עשר בחזקת טהרה, ואמרינן: למאי הלכתא? ואמר רבא: לומר שאם תראה בתוך י"א, אינה מטמאה מעת לעת. ומתניתין קתני: מטמאה מעת לעת, ארישא דקתני: אחר הימים בדקה ומצאה טמאה. ומתמה הש"ס: ולאו אותביניה בפ' בנות כותים (שם), ולא איפרוק:
Rashi on Niddah 68b:2:1.english: To say that she does not transmit ritual impurity for a twenty-four-hour period - In the chapter "Banot Kutim" (above, Niddah 39a), [the mishna] teaches: "All eleven [days are] in the presumption of ritual purity." And we said: For what halakha [is this stated]? And Rava said: To say that if she sees [blood] during the eleven [days], she does not transmit ritual impurity for a twenty-four-hour period. And our mishna teaches: "She transmits ritual impurity for a twenty-four-hour period," [referring] to the first clause, which teaches: "After the days, she examined [herself] and found [herself] impure." And the Gemara wonders: But didn't we refute him in the chapter "Banot Kutim" (ibid.), and it was not resolved?

Rashi on Niddah 68b:4:1.english: When [the mishna] teaches: "And she transmits ritual impurity for a twenty-four-hour period"

Rashi on Niddah 68b:4:2.hebrew: אריש פירקין קאי ראתה ועודה בבית אביה - ב"ה אומרים: כל הלילה שלה, וקאמר דאם ראתה לאחר מכאן, מטמאה מעת לעת:
Rashi on Niddah 68b:4:2.english: It refers to the beginning of our chapter, [to the case where] she saw [blood] while still in her father's house - Beit Hillel say: "The entire night is hers," and [the mishna] is saying that if she saw [blood] after this, she transmits ritual impurity for a twenty-four-hour period.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:5:1.hebrew: כתחלת נדה - כבתולת דמים, דקי"ל (לעיל נדה דף ז.) דיה שעתה בראייה ראשונה:
Rashi on Niddah 68b:5:1.english: Like the beginning of menstruation - Like a virgin with regard to blood, as we hold (above, Niddah 7a): Her time is sufficient upon her first sighting.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:6:1.hebrew: ואם יש לה וסת - קא סלקא דעתך אסיפא דמתני' קאי, דקתני: אחר הימים בדקה ומצאה טמאה — מטמאה מעת לעת, ואם יש לה וסת קבוע לאחר הימים, דהיינו ימי זיבה, וראתה בו — דיה שעתה:
Rashi on Niddah 68b:6:1.english: And if she has a regular period - [The Gemara] initially thought that [this] refers to the latter clause of the mishna, which teaches: [If] after the days [of niddah] she examined [herself] and found [herself] impure, she imparts impurity [retroactively] for a twenty-four-hour period; and if she has an established regular period after the days — that is, the days of zivah — and she saw [blood] during it, her time suffices for her.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:6:2.hebrew: לומר שאינה קובעת - בפ' בנות כותים, גבי כל י"א בחזקת טהרה:
Rashi on Niddah 68b:6:2.english: To say that she does not establish - In the chapter "Banot Kutim," regarding "All eleven [days are] in the presumptive status of purity."

Rashi on Niddah 68b:7:1.hebrew: אמר לך שמואל - כי אמרי אנא לקולא, דלא בעינן תלת זימני למיעקריה, דהא קתני כל י"א בחזקת טהרה, דהיינו קולא, דדמיה מסולקין. אבל לענין דיה שעתה, כל שכן דהוי וסת, דהא דמיה מסולקין:
Rashi on Niddah 68b:7:1.english: Shmuel could say to you - When I said [this, it was] as a leniency: that we do not require three times to uproot it, for it teaches: "All eleven [days are] in a presumptive status of purity," which is a leniency, [meaning] that her blood is removed. But with regard to [the rule of] "her time is sufficient," all the more so is it considered a fixed cycle, since her blood is removed.

Rashi on Niddah 68b:9:1.hebrew: עם סילוק ידיה ראתה - ואפילו הכי אמרת טהורה, הלכך מה לי הפסיקה בטהרה בראשון כו':
Rashi on Niddah 68b:9:1.english: With the removal of her hands she saw [blood] - And even so, you say [she is] pure; therefore, what difference is it to me whether she ceased in purity on the first [day], etc.?

Tosafot on Niddah 68b:12:1.hebrew: אמרו ליה הרי זו בחזקת טהרה - וא"ת: תקשה דרבי יוסי דהכא, דקאמר דסגי לה בהפרשה שחרית, אדרבי יוסי דפרק בא סימן (לעיל נדה דף נג.), דקאמר: ומה אילו נדה שלא הפרישה בטהרה מן המנחה ולמעלה, לא תהא בחזקת טומאה?! אלמא, בעי הפרשה מן המנחה ולמעלה. ויש לומר: דהתם מיירי כשהפרישה ביום שראתה בו שחרית, והכא מיירי בבדקה שחרית ומצאה טהורה. וקשה: דאם כן, כי פרכינן לרבי יהודה: אילו ידיה בעיניה כל בין השמשות וכו' — לימא ר' יוסי לנפשיה! דהא איהו נמי מצריך הפרשה מן המנחה ולמעלה כשהפרישה ביום שראתה; ומה מועיל עיכוב זה? שמא עם סילוק ידיה ראתה! וי"ל: דלנפשיה לא קשה; דכיון דהוחזקה רואה שחרית, דין הוא להצריכה הפרשה מן המנחה ולמעלה, בלא חומרא אלא מן הדין, ואין לנו להחמיר ולספק שמא עם סילוק ידיה ראתה, להצריכה בדיקה בסוף היום. אבל רבי יהודה, שבא להחמיר ולספק — דאפילו בשלא ראתה שחרית, אלא בבדקה עצמה ומצאה טהורה, הוא מצריך הפרשה גם בסוף היום — היה לו להחמיר ולבדוק מספק שמא עם סילוק ידיה ראתה:
Tosafot on Niddah 68b:12:1.english: They said to him: She has a presumptive status of ritual purity - And if you say: Let [the statement of] Rabbi Yosei here, where he says that a separation in the morning is sufficient for her, present a difficulty against [the statement of] Rabbi Yosei in the chapter "Ba Siman" (above, Niddah 53a), where he says: "And what if a menstruating woman did not separate in purity from minḥa onward, would she not have a presumptive status of ritual impurity?!" — evidently, he requires a separation from minḥa onward! And one can say: There, it is dealing with [a case where] she performed the separation on a day on which she had seen [blood] in the morning; whereas here, it is dealing with [a case where] she examined [herself] in the morning and found [herself to be] pure. And it is difficult: For if so, when we raise a challenge against Rabbi Yehuda — "[Only] if her hands were in her 'eyes' [i.e., private parts] for the entire twilight, etc." — let Rabbi Yosei say [this challenge] to himself! For he too requires a separation from minḥa onward when she performs the separation on a day on which she saw [blood], and what does this delay accomplish? Perhaps with the removal of her hands she saw [blood]! And one can say: For himself, it is not difficult; for since she was established as having seen [blood] in the morning, it is the law to require her to perform a separation from minḥa onward — not as a stringency, but as a matter of fundamental law — and we do not need to be [unduly] stringent and raise a doubt that perhaps with the removal of her hands she saw [blood], so as to require her to perform an examination at the end of the day. However, Rabbi Yehuda, who comes to be stringent and raise a doubt — for even where she did not see [blood] in the morning, but rather examined herself and found [herself to be] pure, he requires a separation at the end of the day as well — he should have been stringent to require an examination out of doubt that perhaps with the removal of her hands she saw [blood].

Tosafot on Niddah 68b:21:1.hebrew: אבל הלכה כרבי אליעזר - אע"ג דאין למדין הלכה מפי הש"ס, הא פסקינן בפ"ק לעיל (נדה דף ז:) כרבי אליעזר בארבע, והא חד מינייהו:
Tosafot on Niddah 68b:21:1.english: But the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer - Even though we do not deduce the halakha from the mouth of the Shas, behold, we ruled in the first chapter above (Niddah 7b) in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer in four [cases], and this is one of them.
